name: Indolent Primary Cutaneous B-Cell Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Cutaneous Marginal Zone B-Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of dense, nodular or diffuse infiltrate of neoplastic B-cells in the dermis without epidermotropism
Expression of B-cell markers CD20+, CD79a+, with absence of CD5 and CD10 in marginal zone lymphoma subtype or CD10+ in follicle center lymphoma subtype
Solitary or localized erythematous to violaceous plaques or nodules confined to the skin without extracutaneous involvement
Clonal immunoglobulin gene rearrangement supporting B-cell clonality
No evidence of systemic lymphoma on staging investigations

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of B-cell infiltrate with appropriate immunophenotype and clinical presentation localized to the skin, excluding systemic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, immunophenotypic, and molecular data

pathognomonic.symptomName: Solitary or localized erythematous to violaceous cutaneous nodules
searchTerms: single or localized red-purple skin nodules

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dermal infiltration by neoplastic B-cells without epidermotropism
searchTerms: skin layer involvement without surface spread

common.notes: Often mistaken for benign lesions initially

searchTerms: skin feels thick and firm in one spot

common.symptomName: Slow progression of skin lesions over months to years
Absence of systemic B symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats)

occasional.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas
Mild tenderness on palpation of lesions

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of skin lesions

laboratory: Clonal immunoglobulin gene rearrangement in skin biopsy
imaging: Negative or localized findings on PET-CT or CT scan excluding systemic involvement
genetic: Somatic mutations in genes such as TNFAIP3, MYD88 (in some cases)
other: Histopathology showing nodular or diffuse dermal infiltrate of B-cells without epidermotropism

distinguishingFeatures: Different clinical presentation with patches and plaques
Lack of clonal immunoglobulin gene rearrangement
Spontaneous regression or response to antibiotics

redFlags: Development of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Evidence of extracutaneous dissemination on imaging
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Grange F, Beylot-Barry M. Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphomas: diagnosis and treatment. Curr Opin Oncol. 2013;25(2):176-182.
Orphanet: Indolent primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma. ORPHA:178557.
